items.title: Unconfirmed package installation runs at CLI script import

findings.title: asltk is pip-installed silently at first module run, without user confirmation
findings.explanation: If `asltk` is missing, the CLI script calls `slicer.util.pip_install("asltk==1.1.3")` straight away. This installs asltk and all its transitive dependencies into Slicer's shared Python with no prompt, even though the download may be large. Those dependencies may pin or replace packages Slicer bundles (numpy, scipy, SimpleITK, pydicom), and I did not verify them. The install happens inside a `python-real` subprocess, so the user sees nothing in the UI. The README mentions it only in a note. The `slicer` package may also not be fully usable from `python-real`, so the fallback may simply fail.
findings.suggestion: Add a scripted module with a GUI that tells the user which packages will be installed and asks for confirmation before calling `pip_install`. Check that asltk's dependency requirements do not pin or downgrade Slicer-bundled packages. Apply the same change to the Multi_Echo_ASL script.

findings.title: Scripted CLI modules call `slicer.util.pip_install` inside standalone `python-real` subprocess
findings.evidence:
try:
    from asltk.asldata import ASLData
    from asltk.reconstruction import CBFMapping
    from asltk.utils.io import ImageIO
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    import slicer.util
    slicer.util.pip_install("asltk==1.1.3")
findings.explanation: Both `CBF_ATT_ASL.py` and `Multi_Echo_ASL.py` are configured as `SlicerMacroBuildScriptedCLI` modules running under `#!/usr/bin/env python-real`. When Slicer executes a Scripted CLI module, it launches a standalone `python-real` subprocess rather than executing inside the embedded Slicer Python interpreter. In a standalone `python-real` process, `import slicer.util` is not available (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'slicer'`), so the automatic installation fallback for `asltk==1.1.3` will fail with an unhandled exception whenever `asltk` is not already installed. Furthermore, installing packages silently during CLI execution without prior user confirmation violates Slicer's convention for third-party Python package installation.
findings.suggestion: Either invoke `pip` via `subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "asltk==1.1.3"])` in the `python-real` CLI script, or provide a ScriptedLoadableModule wrapper that asks the user for confirmation before calling `slicer.util.pip_install("asltk==1.1.3")`. Also synchronize the version in `requirements.txt` (`asltk==1.1.0`) with the version installed in the scripts (`asltk==1.1.3`).

findings.title: Unconfirmed package installation runs at CLI script import
findings.evidence:
try:
    from asltk.asldata import ASLData
    from asltk.reconstruction import CBFMapping
    from asltk.utils.io import ImageIO
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    import slicer.util
    slicer.util.pip_install("asltk==1.1.3")
    from asltk.asldata import ASLData
findings.explanation: When the script is imported or executed and an asltk import fails, it immediately downloads and installs asltk and its dependencies into the shared Slicer Python environment, without asking the user. This can change packages used by other extensions; a missing transitive import also triggers the same installation. Multi_Echo_ASL/Multi_Echo_ASL.py:28-37 contains the same pattern. The precise discovery/startup behavior and transitive packages could not be verified.
findings.suggestion: Move dependency installation out of module import into an explicit, informed user-confirmed setup step; inspect its dependencies and avoid modifying Slicer-bundled packages incompatibly.

items.title: Smoothing-parameter validation in CBF module compares wrong case and never triggers

findings.title: Smoothing-parameter validation in CBF module compares wrong case and never triggers
findings.explanation: Valid methods are 'Gaussian' and 'Median', but the checks compare against lowercase 'gaussian' and 'median'. Invalid sigma or kernel sizes, such as an even median size, therefore pass validation and fail later inside asltk or give wrong results. The Multi_Echo module uses the correct case.
findings.suggestion: Compare against 'Gaussian' and 'Median', matching the Multi_Echo module.

findings.title: Smoothing parameter validation in `CBF_ATT_ASL.py` never runs due to case mismatch
findings.explanation: In `CBF_ATT_ASL/CBF_ATT_ASL.py`, `checkUpParameters` validates `args.smoothMethod` against `['None', 'Gaussian', 'Median']` (capitalized), but then checks `if args.smoothMethod == 'gaussian'` (line 187) and `if args.smoothMethod == 'median'` (line 192) in lowercase before `args.smoothMethod` has been lowercased. As a result, invalid smoothing parameters (such as an even or non-positive kernel size for Median filtering) bypass validation in `CBF_ATT_ASL.py`.
findings.suggestion: Check against `'Gaussian'` and `'Median'` (as done in `Multi_Echo_ASL.py` lines 192 and 197) or compare `args.smoothMethod.lower()`.

findings.title: CBF smoothing parameter validation never matches accepted method names
findings.explanation: The accepted and GUI-provided names are capitalized, while the Gaussian and Median validation branches test lowercase strings. Consequently invalid sigma or kernel sizes pass this validation and reach reconstruction, potentially failing or producing unintended smoothing.
findings.suggestion: Normalize the method once before both validation and dispatch, and test invalid Gaussian and Median parameters.

items.title: Documented outputFolder option does not control output location

findings.title: Documented outputFolder option does not control output location
findings.evidence:
print('<filter-progress>0.9</filter-progress>')
  print('<filter-comment>Saving output files...</filter-comment>')
  if args.norm_cbf:
    maps['cbf_norm'].save_image(args.out_cbf)
  else:
    maps['cbf'].save_image(args.out_cbf)
  maps['att'].save_image(args.out_att)
findings.explanation: The XML's command-line example specifies --outputFolder and relative output names, but the script only checks that folder exists and saves directly to the output arguments. Relative names thus resolve against the process working directory, not the selected output folder. The multi-echo script has the same issue.
findings.suggestion: Join relative output paths to the chosen output folder, or remove the option and correct the documentation.

items.title: Mixed vector formats silently truncate timing values

findings.title: Mixed vector formats silently truncate timing values
findings.explanation: If one timing vector is space-separated and another is comma-separated, conversion of the first triggers the fallback, which reads only element zero of both vectors. For example, a comma-separated LD list loses all but its first value. The multi-echo module uses the same fallback for three vectors.
findings.suggestion: Parse each vector independently, supporting the documented separators without discarding elements, and validate its length against the acquisition.

items.title: Overriding `print` with `rich.print` can interfere with Slicer CLI XML progress tags

findings.title: Overriding `print` with `rich.print` can interfere with Slicer CLI XML progress tags
findings.evidence:
import numpy as np
from rich import print
findings.explanation: Both CLI scripts override Python's built-in `print` with `rich.print`. Slicer's CLI process runner parses standard output for XML progress tags such as `<filter-start>`, `<filter-progress>0.1</filter-progress>`, and `<filter-end>`. Because `rich.print` interprets angle-bracket tags as Rich console markup and applies terminal formatting/word wrapping, it can strip or alter the XML progress tags expected by Slicer.
findings.suggestion: Use Python's built-in `print` (and `sys.stdout.flush()`) for Slicer `<filter-...>` XML progress reporting.

items.title: Same silent pip install in the Multi_Echo_ASL module

findings.title: Same silent pip install in the Multi_Echo_ASL module
findings.explanation: The identical pattern is repeated, so either module can trigger a silent installation into the shared environment.
findings.suggestion: Centralize and gate the installation behind a user confirmation.

items.title: Unchecking `normalizedCBF` in the GUI has no effect because omitted CLI boolean flags default to `'true'`

findings.title: Unchecking `normalizedCBF` in the GUI has no effect because omitted CLI boolean flags default to `'true'`
findings.explanation: In Slicer's CLI execution model, `<boolean>` parameters are passed as a flag (`--normalizedCBF`) when checked (`true`) and omitted entirely from the command-line arguments when unchecked (`false`). Because `CBF_ATT_ASL.py` defaults `parsed.get('normalizedCBF', 'true')` to `'true'` when the flag is absent, unchecking "Set CBF to mL/100 g/min scale" in the Slicer GUI still results in `args.norm_cbf == True`. Consequently, users cannot disable CBF normalization from the GUI.
findings.suggestion: Default missing boolean flags to `'false'` (`parsed.get('normalizedCBF', 'false')`) when invoked by Slicer's CLI launcher, or use standard Slicer CLI argument parsing.

items.title: Input images are declared as disk `<file>` parameters rather than scene `<image>` nodes

findings.title: Input images are declared as disk `<file>` parameters rather than scene `<image>` nodes
findings.evidence:
<file fileExtensions=".nii,.nii.gz">
    <name>inputASL</name>
      <label>Input ASL file</label>
      <longflag>inputASL</longflag>
      <description><![CDATA[Input ASL file path in .nii or nii.gz format]]></description>
    </file>
findings.explanation: Both `CBF_ATT_ASL.xml` and `Multi_Echo_ASL.xml` declare `inputASL`, `inputM0`, and `labelMask` as `<file>` parameters restricted to `.nii,.nii.gz` on disk rather than `<image>` parameters, whereas the outputs (`outputCBF`, `outputATT`, `outputVolume`) are declared as `<image channel="output">`. This prevents users from selecting input volumes that are already loaded in the Slicer scene.
findings.suggestion: Consider using `<image>` parameters for input volumes if `asltk` supports the file formats Slicer uses for CLI volume exchange, or document that inputs must be selected as external NIfTI files from disk while outputs are loaded into the scene.

items.title: No tests, no research-use disclaimer; docs and requirements inconsistent; sample data on Google Drive

findings.title: No tests, no research-use disclaimer; docs and requirements inconsistent; sample data on Google Drive
findings.explanation: The repository has no automated tests. `requirements.txt` pins asltk==1.1.0 while the scripts install 1.1.3. The tutorial sample data is on a personal Google Drive link. There is no statement that the maps are for research use only. The catalog entry tracks the moving branch `main`.
findings.suggestion: Align the versions, add a research-use note, host the sample data in a stable location, and consider pinning `scm_revision` to a commit or tag.
